make sure ddflow recommends install for codeguide-mcp companion to use the remote public mcp server, instead of downloading it local (docker) to prevent situations when we use devcontainers, to have docker in docker in the devcontainer.
Also make an investigation will ddflow work well in devcontainers and are there changes needed to support this? Separately, could we produce devcontainer features for ddflow as part of the github pipeline, and publish them in the devcontainer features magazine, so we could have the ability to add ddflow automatically in a devcontainer?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-20: (1) the codeguide-mcp companion must be recommended as the public remote MCP server, not a local docker pull, so a devcontainer never needs docker-in-docker (D-codeguide-remote-default); (2) investigate whether ddflow works well in devcontainers and what has to change; (3) produce devcontainer Features for ddflow in the GitHub pipeline and publish them (GHCR, listed in the containers.dev features index) so ddflow can be added to any devcontainer automatically. Known risks to test, not assume: .claude/settings.json and hooks record absolute interpreter paths of the machine that wrote them (doctor already warns they dangle elsewhere); git worktrees and flock on bind mounts / virtiofs / overlayfs; UID mapping and git safe.directory; ddflow next folds a 65 MB log, slow on mounts; adaptive parallelism and pytest -n auto read host cores/load, not the container's cgroup limits; /proc/locks visibility in a PID namespace; .ddflow/local and secrets do not survive a container rebuild unless in a volume or remoteEnv; LAN reviewer hosts and roborev/kilo reachability from the container network; the pre-commit golang gitleaks build needs go. Publishing is outward-facing: the GHCR package and the containers.dev index submission need the operator's go-ahead (DCF-collection-index is an operator step). Reuse ddflow.infra.container.in_container, the mcpconfig registration, the harness descriptors and the existing publish workflow; do not build a second install path.
data.title: Devcontainers: no docker-in-docker for companions, ddflow verified to work in a devcontainer, and a published devcontainer Feature that installs ddflow

data.body: Today a companion is a local command (companions.toml: command/args/detect/install). Add a remote kind: transport = http (streamable HTTP), url, optional headers/auth reference (never a literal key), a probe that is THREE-VALUED (reachable / unreachable / not probed; unreachable is 'unavailable', never 'absent' and never a pass; offline must not break the gate silently), and the registration form per agent from the harness descriptors: Claude Code (.mcp.json type http + url), Kilo/opencode (type remote), VS Code (servers[..].type http), Cursor (url), Codex/Gemini where supported; agents that only speak stdio get the documented bridge (npx mcp-remote) as an explicit option. registered-detection must match by URL as well as by name (see B-fix-companions-id-entry, R366566d801). Content a remote companion serves into a gate is labelled imported/untrusted guidance. Conformance: every choice is a knob (D-everything-configurable); reuse ddflow.infra.container.in_container, services/mcpconfig registration and the harness descriptors; files under 20 KB; no private addresses or keys in tracked files.
data.title: Companions can be REMOTE MCP servers: an http transport entry, a reachability probe, registration forms per agent

data.body: ddflow.infra.container.in_container() exists. When it is true: ddflow companions and install-companions never print 'docker pull/run' as the install route; they offer the remote or npx/uvx form, or say 'not installable here' with the reason; the recommendation text names the container. Detect devcontainer markers (REMOTE_CONTAINERS, DEVCONTAINER, CODESPACES, /.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv) and cgroup. A knob can override for a container that really has a docker socket. Regression: with the markers faked, no companion recommendation contains 'docker'. Conformance: every choice is a knob (D-everything-configurable); reuse ddflow.infra.container.in_container, services/mcpconfig registration and the harness descriptors; files under 20 KB; no private addresses or keys in tracked files.
data.title: Never recommend a docker-based companion inside a container (devcontainer, Codespaces, CI container)

data.body: Implements D-codeguide-remote-default (operator 2026-10-20). Switch the codeguide companion to the public remote server published in the codeguide-mcp README (https://codeguide-mcp-86057491046.europe-west1.run.app/mcp, streamable HTTP, no authentication); keep the docker image as an explicit local mode ([companions] mode = local, for offline or air-gapped use) that is never offered inside a container. Update the install-companions prompt, mcp_instructions, the README companion table and the doctor/companions text (what is contacted: the guide names asked for, not project code). The standards gate prompt records which source was used (remote or local) in its evidence. Existing registrations of the docker form keep working and are shown as 'local'. Regression: companions on a fresh repo recommends the remote URL; with in_container faked and no docker, it still reports a usable recommendation. Conformance: every choice is a knob (D-everything-configurable); reuse ddflow.infra.container.in_container, services/mcpconfig registration and the harness descriptors; files under 20 KB; no private addresses or keys in tracked files.
data.title: codeguide companion: public remote server by default, docker as an explicit local mode

data.body: Operator 2026-10-20. Docker 29.x is available on the build machine; the devcontainer CLI is not installed (npx @devcontainers/cli or the plain docker equivalent is fine). Build a devcontainer for this repo (python base image + git + uv, workspace as a bind mount, a non-root remoteUser with UID mapping) and test with real runs, marking each CONFIRMED / REFUTED / NOT TESTED: (1) install routes: uvx ddflow, pipx, pip; ddflow --version; ddflow setup/adopt inside; (2) git worktrees and ddflow claim/merge under a bind mount; safe.directory; core.hooksPath and the pre-commit hook; (3) flock/fcntl locks on bind mounts, overlayfs and (documented) macOS virtiofs / Windows WSL2: two agents, one task; the /proc/locks holder diagnosis in a PID namespace; (4) absolute interpreter paths in .claude/settings.json and hooks written on the host dangling inside the container (doctor's note) and the fix (machine-independent launch, ddflow adopt --launch uvx); (5) performance: ddflow next / status on the 65 MB log on a bind mount versus a volume; (6) cpu/memory: os.cpu_count and /proc/loadavg report the HOST, not the cgroup limit; pytest -n auto and the adaptive parallelism governor over-subscribe a limited container: measure with --cpus=2; (7) persistence: .ddflow/local, [REDACTED:path], reviewer config and caches across a container rebuild (volumes, remoteEnv, mounts); (8) network: LAN reviewer hosts, roborev/kilo, the remote codeguide companion, GitHub from the container; MCP stdio servers started inside; (9) docker-in-docker: confirm no ddflow path needs docker once the codeguide default is remote; (10) CI container jobs. Deliver a matrix with the command and its output per cell, the list of required changes as filed tasks (RC-* with globs, needs, wave), and a recommended devcontainer.json for this repo. Falsifier: every cell works unchanged.
data.title: Does ddflow work well in a devcontainer? Build one, run it, list what breaks and what must change

data.body: Feature layout for the devcontainers/action tooling: devcontainer-features/src/ddflow/{devcontainer-feature.json, install.sh}. Options: version (latest or a pin), method (uv|pipx|pip), adopt (agents to register ddflow for; empty = none), companions (remote|none; never docker), enableMcp. installsAfter ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/common-utils, python and git as needed; installs for _REMOTE_USER, idempotent, no secrets, no network calls beyond the package index; leaves PATH correct (containerEnv) and prints the next step. Uses the machine-independent launch from RC-devcontainer-research (not absolute interpreter paths). Unit tests lint the JSON schema and shellcheck the script.
